summary: Mount Diablo — a 3,849-foot peak visible from nearly every corner of the county — is one of the few summits in the world from which you can see more total land area than any other point on Earth except Mount Kilimanjaro, a claim the U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey once promoted and that still draws hikers to its summit for views stretching from the Sierra Nevada to the Farallon Islands. That landmark anchors a county of striking internal contrasts: the western cities along the Bay — Richmond, Martinez, the Walnut Creek–Concord corridor — operate as both job centers and BART-connected commuter feeders into San Francisco, while the eastern reaches flatten into delta farmland and wind-turbine ridgelines near the Altamont Pass. At a median household income of roughly $125,700 against an $830,800 median home price, the price-to-income ratio lands around 6.6×, steep but notably below neighboring Alameda or San Francisco counties. Major employers span Chevron's refinery operations in Richmond, the John Muir Health system, county government, and a growing logistics sector near the Interstate 80 and Highway 4 corridors. With 9.4 hours of daily sunshine and average highs around 70°F, the inland valleys run 10–15 degrees warmer than the fog-cooled bayfront towns — a microclimate split that means choosing your city within the county is almost as consequential as choosing the county itself.
